full_page.content:
c. 1950
The following is a faithful transcription of typed notes by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F. M.Cap.
RECOMMENDATIONS.
First and simplest: Is the known fact that the bitter- enemies of God and Religion have been alos the most persistently bitter opponents of this work. The devil himself tried every way in his power to preven its being written in the first place; and withhim ever since its first appearance, his visible agents -- out- standingly the jansenist and atheistic members of the Parisian Sorbonne - have in every way possible, hind- ered its circulation.
Hence, its warmest friends and staunchest defenders from among the most zealous of the Bishops, the Cardinals, the Generals of differ- ent orders, Catholic universities and Popes them- selves, from Innocent XI and Clement XI down. So that such recommendations would fill a good sized volume themselves.
But better than any of these, or perhaps all of them together, if studied in the light of faith and confident heart with which the writer must have written it, is the simple but masterly introductions by the humble writer herself, - most privileged disciple and actual Secretary in the writing of this climax-compendium at once of sacred history, of moral and dogmatic and of ascetic and mistic theology; the life - Nay more the autobiography of the Queen of the universe.
